newsitem.title: UK: China raises 500 mln marks with five-year Eurobond.
newsitem.headline: China raises 500 mln marks with five-year Eurobond.

text.p: China on Thursday raised 500 million marks ($290 million) in the international capital markets with the launch of a five-year Eurobond, joint lead manager Credit Suisse First Boston said.
The terms of the deal, China's first mark Eurobond after a 10-year absence from the mark sector, were in line with those being touted earlier in the week.
The bond was priced to yield 55 basis points over German government bonds, the bottom end of the 55-60 b.p. range mentioned over the past few days.
It was the first transaction for China this year, and the first since it was upgraded by Standard and Poor's in May. China is rated A3 by Moody's and BBB+ by S&P.
Investor focus is also on the handover of Hong Kong to China -- now only 12 days away.
At a presentation to bankers in London this week, China said it wanted to establish itself with European investors ahead of the planned single currency.

Other objectives of the transaction were to set a benchmark and to fund infrastructure projects, Zhu Guang Yao, deputy director general of the state debt management department of the Ministry of Finance said.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell was the other joint lead manager.
-- Dan Lalor, London newsroom +44 171 542 8863 ($ = 1.731 German Marks)
